genre_note:
302 notes across 30 sub-plans. The cluster splits into three genres that decompose very differently.

(1) Reported features and interviews (doc_0458, 0465, 0468, 0511, 0528, 0549, 0551, 0593, 0598, 0599, 0608, 0099, 0169, 0524). These behave as expected: dominated by empirical_observation (dated events, figures, named testimony) with concept notes for entities (Gaza Sky Geeks, Alliance DAO's eight portfolio startups, the MIT Leg Lab, the "third place"). argument/counter_argument appear where a source stakes a claim with grounds — the UK climate op-ed (doc_0599) is almost entirely argument, and Pebble's post-mortem (doc_0593) yields a clean argument/counter_argument pair (moderation worked / it went too far into "kindness"). model is used only where the source actually traces a mechanism: Meta's GDPR-consent chain, the Twitter-alternative network-effect explanation, Amazon's ML flow/fleet stack, cars-and-robotics convergence.

hypothesis occurs exactly once in the whole cluster and is not manufactured: doc_0593 block 8 states Pebble's founding hypothesis verbatim ("consumers were hungry for a Twitter alternative that prioritized trust, safety and moderation"), and the article then reports it disconfirmed. Everything else that looks forward-looking (OpenAI's chip ambitions, Valve's "successive generations of handhelds", Musk's 250k Cybertrucks/year) is a reported corporate statement, so it is empirical_observation. procedure occurs once (the Apple gift-card + Amazon-credit offer, which is a coupon-code procedure). No navigation notes were produced.

(2) Newsletter roundups (doc_0514, doc_0537 — TechCrunch's The Station). These are the case the brief warns about: two ~1,500–2,000-word documents holding roughly fifty unrelated items. They were decomposed item-by-item (50 notes over five sub-plans), never merged by section. Their section scaffolding ("Micromobbin'", "Deal of the week", "Autonomous vehicles", tip-line boilerplate, host handoffs) is the bulk of the dropped blocks. Convoy and Flexport are the load-bearing cross-document entities here: Convoy's collapse is reported in doc_0514 and its afterlife (Flexport acquiring the technology) in doc_0537, and Flexport's 20%/600-person layoff is stated in both, so flexport_leadership_change_and_layoffs carries blocks from each.

(3) Deals roundups (doc_0091, 0104, 0222, 0404 — Engadget). Four documents, ~11k words, ~120 notes. Coherence forced per-product notes: doc_0222 alone is 53 unrelated items. The decisive structural fact is that the same products recur across all four articles at different sale events, so 21 product notes are shared rather than duplicated — apple_airpods_pro_2nd_gen_holiday_deal draws on doc_0091, doc_0104, doc_0222 and doc_0404; apple_watch_series_9, apple_airtags, mac_mini_m2, ipad_air_m1 and others span three. Writing separate Black Friday and Cyber Monday notes would have split exactly the evidence a cross-article question needs (e.g. the Apple Watch Ultra 2, which is one of the few Apple products whose price went UP from Black Friday's $730 to Cyber Monday's $739 — a fact that only exists inside a shared note).

Coverage: the reported features run 95–99% assigned. The two newsletters land near 90% (~10% is section headers and tip-line/subscribe boilerplate). The four deals articles are the honest shortfall at roughly 88–90%: each carries a 35-word affiliate disclosure, a 58-word Yahoo cross-promotion footer, ~25 two-to-five-word product sub-headers, and a dozen "Read our full review" / "Check out our guide" links — all chrome, but enough of it to hold those documents just under the 90% target. Nothing substantive was dropped from them.

Two dropped-block judgement calls went the other way, per the warning about corrections: doc_0598 block 42 ("This piece was later edited to include relevant information about the attacks by Hamas") was ASSIGNED to israel_hamas_war_october_2023_context rather than discarded, because it is a scope condition on the article's framing; and doc_0528 blocks 41–42, Brady's non-answer on whether Amazon buys or leases Agility robots ("no one-size-fits-all… [Amazon declined to comment further]"), were assigned to the Innovation Fund note rather than dropped as contentless, since the refusal is itself the reported state of the arrangement.
